I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. Here's the configuration:

## Server Setup

**1. Create the bare git repository:**
```bash
mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
git init --bare
```

**2. Create the web root directory:**
```bash
mkdir -p /var/www/html
```

**3. Set up the post-receive hook** (this auto-deploys on push):

Create `/git/server/hooks/post-receive` with:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
GIT_WORK_TREE=/var/www/html git checkout -f
```

Make it executable:
```bash
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

**4. Initialize the web directory** (so first checkout works):
```bash
cd /var/www/html
git init
git remote add origin /git/server
git fetch origin
git checkout -b master origin/master 2>/dev/null || true
```

**5. Set up a web server on port 8080**

Using Python (simplest for testing):
```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

Or with nginx, create `/etc/nginx/sites-available/default`:
```nginx
server {
    listen 8080;
    root /var/www/html;
    index index.html;
}
```

Then restart: `sudo systemctl restart nginx`

## Client Usage

From your local machine:
```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server my-repo
cd my-repo
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then test:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
# Output: hello world
```

The post-receive hook automatically checks out the pushed code to `/var/www/html`, so it appears on the web server immediately.

I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. Here's the configuration:

## Server Setup

**1. Create the bare git repository:**
```bash
mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
git init --bare
```

**2. Create the web root directory:**
```bash
mkdir -p /var/www/html
```

**3. Set up the post-receive hook** (this auto-deploys on push):

Create `/git/server/hooks/post-receive` with:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
GIT_WORK_TREE=/var/www/html git checkout -f
```

Make it executable:
```bash
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

**4. Initialize the web directory** (so first checkout works):
```bash
cd /var/www/html
git init
git remote add origin /git/server
git fetch origin
git checkout -b master origin/master 2>/dev/null || true
```

**5. Set up a web server on port 8080**

Using Python (simplest for testing):
```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

Or with nginx, create `/etc/nginx/sites-available/default`:
```nginx
server {
    listen 8080;
    root /var/www/html;
    index index.html;
}
```

Then restart: `sudo systemctl restart nginx`

## Client Usage

From your local machine:
```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server my-repo
cd my-repo
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then test:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
# Output: hello world
```

The post-receive hook automatically checks out the pushed code to `/var/www/html`, so it appears on the web server immediately.
